 Would Federal Retirees Get a Requested $1,400 Senior Stimulus?
 November 21, 2026 My Federal Retirement 
 The Senior Citizens League (TSCL), a senior advocacy group, is asking the incoming Congress to authorize a one-time $1,400 payment for Social Security recipients.
 The Social Security Administration (SSA) announced a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) for 2027 on October 14, 2026. The first payments reflecting the increase arrive on December 31 for some beneficiaries and in January for most.
 What The Senior Citizens League is asking for
 The request appears in a November 10, 2026, news release from TSCL titled “Seniors Call on the Next Congress to Prioritize Social Security.” The group also released its first forecast for the 2028 COLA, projecting a 3.6% increase, the same as the official 2027 adjustment. TSCL asked the 120th Congress, which begins in January, to take four actions.
 Send a one-time $1,400 payment to help seniors cover rising costs that TSCL says recent COLAs have failed to keep up with
 Expand Medicare to cover dental, vision and hearing care
 Reverse the Medicare and Medicaid cuts that TSCL attributes to the One Big Beautiful Bill
 Raise or remove the cap on earnings subject to Social Security payroll taxes, which is $184,500 in 2026 and, according to SSA, rises to $192,300 in 2027
 TSCL’s November release gives no cost estimate or detailed eligibility rules for the payment. An earlier TSCL open letter from October 2025 called for the same amount and described it as relief for Social Security beneficiaries.
 Where the request stands in Congress
 As of November 21, 2026, Congress has not authorized the $1,400 payment, and no payment is scheduled.

 TSCL asked Congress for the same $1,400 in 2021 , but that campaign did not lead to a separate payment for seniors. The amount matches the maximum per eligible person in the third round of pandemic-era stimulus payments. TSCL’s 2025 letter pointed to earlier relief payments as precedent.
 Would federal retirees get the payment?
 Eligibility would depend on how Congress wrote the law. Federal Employees Retirement System (FERS) employees generally earn Social Security credits through their federal service, but a FERS retiree would qualify for a payment tied to Social Security only if they received a benefit that met the law’s requirements. Some Civil Service Retirement System (CSRS) retirees qualify for Social Security through other work or on a spouse’s record. Those who receive no Social Security benefit could be left out unless Congress included a separate provision.
 In 2009, Congress provided for both groups. The Congressional Research Service (CRS) reported that ARRA provided a $250 payment to eligible Social Security beneficiaries and several other groups, along with a $250 refundable tax credit for certain government retirees who did not receive the payment. The Internal Revenue Service (IRS) explained how the economic recovery payment and the separate tax credit worked. TSCL’s November release does not address retirees who receive no Social Security benefit.

 The 2008 and 2009 payments were part of the response to the Great Recession. The 2020 and 2021 payments were part of the federal response to the pandemic. TSCL’s latest request comes as Social Security beneficiaries are set to receive their largest COLA since 2023.
 When to expect the first 2027 COLA payment
 The 2027 Social Security COLA applies to December 2026 benefits, which most beneficiaries receive in January. For SSI, the increase applies to the January 2027 payment, which arrives early. The Social Security payment date depends on the beneficiary’s payment schedule and, for most beneficiaries, a birthday. SSA’s 2027 payment schedule shows the regular payment dates.

 December 31 is the early payment date for January SSI and for December Social Security benefits normally paid on January 3. New Year’s Day is a federal holiday, and January 3 falls on a Sunday. Account holders can view their personalized COLA notices in my Social Security starting in late November. SSA set November 18 as the deadline for people without an account to create one and enroll in paperless notices to see the notice online. Everyone else receives a paper notice in the mail during December. CSRS and FERS annuitants can check their Office of Personnel Management (OPM) online accounts for the updated amounts. OPM’s COLA frequently asked questions explain the rates and eligibility rules, including prorated increases for recent retirees. OPM also explains when the adjustment first appears in annuity payments .
